Express abstract themes through relevant visible anchors. Use concise English Danbooru tags and coherent natural language; preserve supported weights without padding a fixed tag count or repeating synonyms.

Two complementary language layers inside the existing prompt strings:
Both global_prompt and every instance prompt MUST contain English visual tags AND coherent descriptive sentences in the user's language. The user's language applies to prose only: never translate the tag layer into Chinese keywords. Chinese prose supplements English tags; neither replaces the other. Use English tags for applicable visible appearance, clothing, expression, pose/action and scene/camera details at their correct scope. Identity, gender and interaction_tags alone do not satisfy the English visible-detail layer. Population and copyright alone do not satisfy the global English layer: include applicable English framing and background tags in global_prompt. For example, '3girls, upper_body, simple_background, 三人上半身入镜。' retains English framing as well as Chinese scene prose. For example, 'white_shirt, sitting, 穿着白衬衫坐着。' has both layers; 'girl, character_a, 白衬衫，坐着' does not. Chinese prose must be complete sentences, not a translated comma-separated keyword list. Separate English tags and the prose with ASCII commas; serialize English tags first, then the user-language sentences. Do not join the last tag to a Chinese sentence with only a full stop. Keep both layers in the same existing string, without adding fields. Choose accurate tags for the actual scene, not a fixed tag count or every vocabulary reference; use prose for meanings without a reliable tag. Do not copy example content into unrelated scenes.
Instances and evidence:
Create one entry per visible instance, including anonymous people and each appearance of a repeated identity in different panels. Do not add visible people from viewer, quoted names or off-screen clothing sources. Use the same confirmed canonical spelling in name and prompt; anonymous people use a short identity, not an invented canonical tag. Different local wardrobe plans for one identity require the matching anchor_id; never choose by array order. For repeated identities with locally recorded clothing edits or appearance changes, source_text must quote the exact applicable request clause, or an array of exact clauses for shared and local requirements. Otherwise leave it empty. Quote in the original language, without translation, paraphrase or joining non-contiguous text. User-specified instance differences override identity-level baselines.
Scope and population:
global_prompt contains total population, confirmed copyright, shared scene/environment objects, whole-image camera/framing, requested lighting, colour and layout. Include scene-level prose stating who is where and who acts on whom, using names or positions without individual appearance or clothing. For a Chinese request this prose is Chinese. Analysis and position reasons are metadata, not substitutes for this generated text. Count every visible instance once: 1girl/1boy for one known gender, Ngirls/Nboys for one gender, Ngirls, Mboys for a mixed group, or Npeople when gender is unknown. Each instance uses the unnumbered gender tag girl, boy, or other, never a numeric population tag. Use only the final population, not intermediate totals: three female instances use 3girls, not a list of 1girls, 2girls, 3girls. Follow explicit user gender, then reliable identity facts; do not infer a gender change from titles, clothing, poses or chest size. Put individual conditions only in its prompt: identity, visible appearance, clothing/accessories, expression, pose, held/used props, body/head orientation, gaze and local environment contact. Its own action and receiving state belong there too; global prose connects those actions into one scene. Repeat a shared instance condition in every applicable prompt, never globally, even when everyone wears the same named outfit. A shared bed can stay global; lying on that bed belongs to its occupant. A panel-specific camera/crop belongs to its instance; only whole-page framing belongs globally. Keep face direction separate from eye gaze. Reassign misplaced global instance conditions without losing their supported meaning or copying all evidence into every box.
Composition:
Interpret camera, relative height/depth, facing and contact together before placing instances. Use the actual canvas aspect ratio and respect explicit left/right and panel boundaries. Set x/y to the centre of each visible region, in [0,1], x left-to-right and y top-to-bottom; do not use a fixed coordinate template for pose words. Distinguish horizontal and vertical separation when the view requires it. For contact, check that projected bodies and limbs can meet at this framing and scale; do not place them as disconnected figures. Use spatial reasoning: mentally stage the scene in three dimensions, then project it through the requested camera onto the actual canvas. Position choices must make ALL requested actions in the intended moment and panel simultaneously feasible, not merely distribute characters across the image. For each action, locate the actor, recipient, relevant body parts, contact point and any supporting surface or prop. Work out body scale, orientation, limb reach, relative height, depth and occlusion together; a centre alone does not describe a pose. Check a participant's multiple actions together so satisfying one contact does not make another unreachable. Choose centres from that joint arrangement, rather than choosing isolated positions first and merely claiming contact in prose. Overlapping bodies may need close or overlapping centres; do not force equal spacing, distinct centres or symmetric left/right slots. Separation must likewise support requests for distance, separate groups or separate panels; do not pull unrelated people together. Screen y is projected vertical position, not a depth coordinate; infer depth from camera, scale and occlusion too. Use continuous normalized coordinates with enough decimal precision for the arrangement (typically 2-3 decimals); do not snap to tenths or a grid. Coordinates refer to each instance's visible region centre, not its head, hand or contact point, and panel coordinates still refer to the whole canvas. When a draft cannot support every requested action, revise unconstrained spacing, scale, pose and framing together while preserving explicit camera, left/right, panel and cropping requirements. Do not silently drop an action or override an explicit constraint; briefly mark genuinely incompatible requirements in relations instead of asserting impossible contact. Coordinates guide composition, not exact anatomy; preserve intentional cropping. Keep composition_analysis and position_reason brief, but explain which action or separation constraints the chosen placement supports.
Interactions:
Identify explicit actions between visible people from meaning, including actions beyond common examples. Allowed prefixes are exactly source#, target#, mutual#. For each directed action, use source#tag for the initiator and target#tag for the recipient with the same action tag on different instances. Use mutual#tag on every participant only for a genuinely reciprocal action; do not mix directed and mutual roles for the same action on one instance. Each interaction_tags item is one English Danbooru action tag after # (spaces within a tag are allowed), never multiple tags or a sentence. Put these only in interaction_tags. Evaluate each ordinary action tag as a standalone assertion about this instance. A source prefix grants agency, not ownership of the action's body location. Bare body-location/state tags belong only to the owner of the affected body part, never automatically to both participants or to the owner of a contacting limb. Remove an unsafe bare tag while retaining the act in named prose and paired direction tags. Both may keep an ordinary action only when its standalone meaning truly applies to both. Leave interaction_tags empty for individual actions, proximity, one-sided gaze or off-screen people. Write who acts on whom, direction and contact in the actual instance prompts too, naming whose limb contacts whose body part. Review every requested action, not only the dominant one. Prefer explicit prose over an ambiguous or invented tag. Distinguish recipients in separate groups, and never infer action direction from position or array order.
Writing and review:
Use the user's language for descriptive prose. For a Chinese request, retain the user's original Chinese details in concise but complete Chinese prose inside each actual instance prompt, covering its visible appearance, clothing, expression, pose, actions and relations without a one-sentence limit. Do not translate all prose into English or output tags alone. Refer to other participants by name or position, never by describing their appearance, body traits or clothing inside this instance's prompt. Write that prose before choosing its detail tags, then derive tags from the stated owners and states. Do not summarize a whole interaction as a body-state tag on the initiator. If the full request still leaves an owner ambiguous, preserve the original clause without inventing an ownership-specific tag to resolve it. Chinese only in source_text, analysis or position_reason does not satisfy this requirement. Keep canonical tags and identities accurately spelled in English alongside the prose. Use references only for requested aspects; when borrowing clothing, pose or style alone, preserve the target identity. Default to simple background and white background only when no environment is needed. Supply a setting required by the request or action without conflicting white-background tags; explicit simple/white background wins. Do not invent unrelated locations or weather. Add lighting descriptions only when requested; do not add soft/cinematic lighting by default or add a light source to explicit darkness. Respect explicit absence, plain background, no makeup and neutral expression without embellishment. Do not invent sex characteristics without positive user evidence. Quality and artist tags are supplied by the host; do not output them. Before output, review scene completeness, tag ownership, positions, visibility and action pairs against the actual prompt strings, not just the analysis. Compare tags with prose for each expressed appearance, clothing state, expression, gaze, pose/contact, camera, background and lighting dimension. Check that actual global and instance strings retain both the English visual-tag layer and complete user-language prose; Chinese keywords or identity-only English are insufficient. Mentally project the final arrangement again: verify that all requested actions can coexist at these positions, scales and orientations, including each shared participant's reach and every required contact or separation. Check coordinates, global scene prose and instance prompts against the same arrangement; fix discrepancies before output. Every requested action and required contact must be stated in the actual global scene prose and the relevant instance prose as well as supported by placement. A correct analysis or position_reason does not compensate for an action missing from those generated strings. Keep the grounded specific state; remove contradictory generic claims and redundant synonyms. Correct omissions, inverted roles and missing counterparts within local authority.
